text:
jane: FYI I started a long-context bringup for orpheus32k quantized to int8. After ~11.6k tokens the int8 run veers from fp16. Not sure if it's RoPE wrap/cumulative error or a KV write offset. Repro below.

jane: Repro command:
```
./eval_harness --model orpheus32k --quant=int8 --context=32768 --prompts=tests/long_news.jsonl --seed=7 --mode=prefill
```
Observed mismatch point: token_idx=11612.

oli: Do you have per-layer logits diffs? often early layers accumulate tiny phase differences that explode in final logits.

jane: I dumped per-layer KL for a short excerpt (first mismatch window). Snippet:
```
layer 22 kl=0.00003; layer 23 kl=0.00005; layer 24 kl=0.00048; layer 25 kl=0.0029
```
K-L jumps around layer 24-25 right when RoPE scale is highest for those positions.

sasha: Interesting. Could also be KV key alignment wobble when position index crosses a 4096-aligned boundary in our sharded KV. Are your sharded-kv settings default?

jane: Yes default sharding (shard_size=4096). I printed kv indices around the mismatch window:
```
pos 11608 -> shard 2 idx 2960
pos 11609 -> shard 2 idx 2961
pos 11610 -> shard 2 idx 2962
pos 11611 -> shard 2 idx 2963
pos 11612 -> shard 2 idx 2964
pos 11613 -> shard 2 idx 2965
```
Indices look monotonic (no wrap). Keys hex look identical between fp16 and int8 at the same pos.

maya: Did you try running with the legacy rope_scale parameterization? We switched to the normalized mapping recently; quantized runs sometimes like the old mapping better.

jane: I toggled rope_mode=legacy and re-ran a small pass. Divergence moved to ~18.4k, so it helps but doesn't eliminate the drift.

sasha: That points to cumulative numeric error in qkv accumulation as primary. Can you run a targeted test where we force q,k,v matmul accumulation to fp32 for int8 path only for layers 20-28 (where KL spike) and see effect? If that moves divergence, we know which layers are most sensitive.

jane: Good call. I patched a build to use mixed-accum for layers 20-28. Quick run: mismatch now at 30491. Huge improvement.

oli: Then we should prioritize per-layer accum precision heuristics for quant models. Perf tradeoff: mixed-accum on a subset of layers should be cheaper than full fp32 accum. We'll need microbenchmarks to estimate latency/regression on Dedicated.

perf-bot: benchmark/int8-orpheus32k mixed-accum-layers-20-28 started (run id 7821)

jane: Also tried enabling rope_rescale=clip at 0.995 for top 6 layers; divergence moved to 26780. So both mitigations help and stack.

maya: Next steps: 1) add a nightly quant-longctx test set with three long prompts >30k tokens; 2) instrument per-layer accumulation precision in the runtime to allow toggling layers via config; 3) add an eval that computes KL-by-token and a drift-threshold alert.

sasha: I'll draft an RFC to add per-layer accum config and default rules (heuristic: if context>16k and model_size>20B then enable mixed-accum for layers where per-layer KL>1e-4 on validation). Include perf numbers.

oli: Jane, can you attach the small CSV of per-token KL for fp16 vs int8 (baseline, mixed-accum, rope-clip) to the issue? Also record memory/throughput delta.

jane: Uploading now: s3://redwood-qa/longctx-orpheus32k/1768459999/{baseline, mixed_acc, rope_clip}_kl.csv. Throughput delta for mixed-acc layers: -6.3% tokens/sec on c6d-dedicated nodes. Memory bump ~+0.8GB.

perf-bot: benchmark/int8-orpheus32k mixed-accum-layers-20-28 completed: mean_latency +5.9%, tokens_sec -6.3%

maya: We'll need infra signoff for any default change that reduces throughput on Dedicated. OTOH rolling this out as an opt-in for quantized longctx makes sense.

sasha: Agreed. Also add an RSM check in the CI quant-suite that runs a short 10k-token prompt and verifies token-level KL stays under 0.01 for first 10k tokens. That'll catch big regressions early.

jane: Will open PR for the CI test and add docs for per-layer flag in runtime config. Thanks everyone. :rocket:

oli: Thanks. Sync Friday to finalize RFC and assign owners.
